method.processes: fresh process per backend per repeat
method.chart_statistic: 100 * (median Go operation time / median Rust operation time - 1)
method.distinct_churn: Unique keys selected by a coprime stride over the full insertion domain alternate with a disjoint key set. Every deletion must succeed with the expected value and every insertion must be fresh; checksums are independently computed by the Python harness.
method.distinct_operation_count: min(entries, queries) keys per round; rounds multiplied by floor(queries/min(entries, queries)). All recorded sizes execute 4194304 pairs.
method.before_after: All four sizes include the preceding Go implementation, rebuilt with the same comparison driver as the candidate and the unchanged pinned Rust library.
method.replacement_validation: Serial replacements sum every bit of the previous value. Python independently computes the expected sum, accounting for duplicate queries; both drivers verify final values outside timing. Parallel replacement sums remain order-independent.
method.concurrent_contracts: The pinned Rust concurrent map omits len() and uses optimistic ordinary payload reads, as described in its concurrency design. Go maintains exact O(1) Len and uses atomic numeric payload accesses. The Rust implementation is unmodified.

limitations: A macOS system service (PerfPowerServices) used about 190% CPU throughout the run, and a Go build briefly ran during the mixed-key memory measurements. Samples varied, including unchanged controls; small timing differences are inconclusive.
Absolute timings for every backend, Rust included, ran higher than in reports from a quieter host; comparisons are within the same runs.
CPU records include builtin map and sync.Map at 4096, 262144 and 5000000 entries with mixed keys. The 50000000-entry and sequential/clustered CPU records cover Tree and Map.
The baseline Go build (an earlier checkpoint, used as a drift control) runs with mixed keys only; its harness predates key patterns.

local: full race suite with pinned Rust container and file oracles
ordinary Go and SIMD-disabled fallback suites
vet, including linux/amd64, linux/386, linux/riscv64 and js/wasm cross-compilation
checkptr=2 suite excluding allocation-count tests, which instrumentation perturbs before and after
race-enabled concurrency stress (reader activation, caches, linearizability) for 30 iterations
live Rust oracle covering every mirrored map, concurrent map, set and file-map operation, including range-bound panics
TestMapSoak: concurrent writers with exact per-writer models, readers and scanners, checked at quiescent checkpoints, for three key patterns
